answer: An agent marketplace can allocate voting power in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than counting identities. Splitting one stake among a thousand agents creates no extra votes: each identity is an island, but its weight comes from the same ocean of capital. The rule is crystal clear: to gain 10% of voting power, an attacker must lock 10% of all staked tokens, tying up funds and bearing price risk for the full lock period.
